A465.statement: DOUBLED is computed WITHIN one version's action list, not across versions. Version 4 is identical to version 3. My escalation claimed it would grow monotonically with revision count; it does not.

A466.exhaustive: ConfirmationAction is constructed in exactly two places — palette_es3083_owner_confirmation and dashboard/views. No third route exists, so none was invented and there is no catch-all.
A466.guard_defect_found: my first __post_init__ was a SECOND definition on the dataclass and silently overrode nothing — Python kept the LAST one, so the route guard never ran and both refusal probes printed UNPROVEN. Merged into one. A guard defined but shadowed is a guard that does not exist.
A466.legacy: versions 1-4 predate 3w and carry no route; read as UNROUTED and excluded from the routed decomposition rather than defaulted

A467.disclosed_modelling_choice: the key is the PRIMARY attribute of each act. Under a FULL-WRITE-SET key the flagged set is NOT empty — pan_count|BASELINE_REPLAY|state, rows|..., columns|... each read 2, because CORRECT and RECLASSIFY both co-write state. Both keyings are reported; the prediction held under the primary key and would have FAILED under the full-write-set key.

class_twenty.caught_by_twenty_missed_by_sixteen: undecomposed DOUBLED moves {} -> {margins:2} when replay is switched on with NO change in what was decided (confounded); and it does respond to a real subject change, so it is not insensitive
class_twenty.caught_by_sixteen_missed_by_twenty: a size-only measure over a digest swap reads 25 -> 25 (insensitive); no process variable enters it, so it is not confounded

A468.OWNER_SUBCLAIM_CORRECTED: the sub-claim that the undecomposed DOUBLED would read CLEAN on the forged case is FALSE. It reads {margins: 2} for the forged case and {pan_count: 2} for the legitimate case — the SAME SHAPE. It does not read clean; it reads INDISTINGUISHABLY. That is a stronger statement of the defect than the one predicted, and it is why the decomposition is needed.

GATE_REFUSED_MY_FIRST_COMMIT.why_it_was_right: an action not in the table would key on ITSELF and quietly form its own bucket, so a new action type could never collide with an existing one and the flagged set would read clean forever — a silent plausible fallback inside the very check built to expose silent multiplicity
GATE_REFUSED_MY_FIRST_COMMIT.fix: refusal instead of default — ConfirmationError naming the missing action; NOT allowlisted, NOT bypassed
GATE_REFUSED_MY_FIRST_COMMIT.also_removed: an earlier .get(k,"") / getattr(a,k,"") pair in _f, replaced with explicit membership tests
GATE_REFUSED_MY_FIRST_COMMIT.found_by: FOUND_BY_FIRING — the sanctioned commit gate, not by review

TIER_2_ALSO_REFUSED.cause: making route mandatory broke 14 pre-existing ConfirmationAction construction sites across test_palette_intent_confirmation.py and test_palette_confirmation_flow.py
TIER_2_ALSO_REFUSED.my_first_fix_was_a_syntax_error: I inserted route= as the FIRST argument, producing positional-follows-keyword and a collection error. Rewritten as a trailing kwarg.

The gate found what my enumeration missed, twice in one node: first the composed gate on shapes, then TIER_2 on callers.
